## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

The *Revatabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 7), translated as *The History of the Buddha Revata*, is the seventh chapter of the *Buddhavaṁsa* in the Pali Canon [SuttaCentral]. It presents the traditional verse biography and legendary account of Revata, one of the past Buddhas venerated in the Theravāda lineage tradition [SuttaCentral].

Computational analysis via DharmaNexus reveals widespread Pali-internal textual reuse, with 373 matching passages detected across 27 canonical and paracanonical works [DharmaNexus]. The largest concentration of text sharing occurs with the commentary, the *Buddhavaṃsa-aṭṭhakathā*, which accounts for 141 matches totaling over 12,000 characters [DharmaNexus]. The verse narrative also shares repetitive structural and formulaic passages with other *Buddhavaṁsa* accounts, especially the *Sobhitabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 8), *Sumedhabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 13), *Sumanabuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 6), *Sikhībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 22), and *Vipassībuddhavaṁsa* (Bv 21) [DharmaNexus]. Furthermore, DharmaNexus identifies low-to-moderate cross-language computational alignments with Sanskrit and Tibetan Buddhist literature, including the Sanskrit *Saṃghāṭa Sūtra* and *Lalitavistara*, as well as Tibetan versions of Mahāyāna scriptures such as the *Bhadrakalpikāsūtra* (D 94); however, these represent formulaic segment reuse rather than curated textual parallels [DharmaNexus]. SuttaCentral records no curated historical parallels, though it catalogues two translations in two modern languages [SuttaCentral].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
